mission: Build a practical Stephanos VR analysis workspace that turns flat-to-VR research into reusable conversion patterns with Starfield as a primary target.
overview: This lab captures engine, camera, rendering, input, HUD, and performance findings for seated-first VR conversion work.
Cockpit Mode is the pragmatic default: head-tracked seated play with low-friction control mapping and comfort-first frame pacing.
Use this surface as the operational front door while the repo folders hold durable notes, experiments, and tools.

stephanosResponsibilities: discover goals, dependencies, and missing capabilities
coordinate research, build, execution, and verification
return evidence and escalate only genuine judgment or permission gates
captainModel.governingPrinciple: The captain commands the ship; the captain does not carry messages between decks or perform repeatable engineering rituals.

spatialBridge.surfaceRole: A thin spatial command client over the same canonical Stephanos brain, never a separate VR Stephanos.
spatialBridge.visualDirection: An original Stephanos far-future starship bridge: calm, panoramic, seated-first, luminous, mission-led, and not a replica of a specific set.

initialInteractionModel.attention: Quest 3 head tracking and gaze context

readinessGates: canonical continuity across chats, devices, restarts, and agents
capability discovery with available, missing, blocked, and unproven states
Shared Agent Workspace truth for goals, dependencies, actions, blockers, and evidence
authenticated and independently stoppable Battle Bridge control
idempotent execution across duplicate events and reconnects
spatialBridge.primaryReadinessTest: The headset can disconnect completely without losing mission state, approvals, execution state, or evidence.
spatialBridge.implementationGate: Do not begin execution-capable spatial integration until Stephan judges Stephanos intelligent and dependable enough to understand the operating context and safely close the gap between intent and reality.

targets.name: Starfield
targets.mode: Cockpit Mode (controller-based VR) first, then assisted VR
targets.focus: Camera injection, stereo rendering, UI/HUD anchoring, VorpX behavior, performance constraints.

targets.name: Red Dead Redemption 2
targets.focus: Rendering pipeline constraints and reusable module extraction.

knowledgeBuckets: VR Mode Type (Cockpit, Assisted, Motion Control Viability)

techniques.name: Camera Injection
techniques.goal: Stabilize head-tracked seated camera behavior without breaking core gameplay loops.

techniques.name: Stereo Rendering
techniques.goal: Assess depth reconstruction and stereo strategies for non-native VR pipelines.

techniques.name: Tooling Integration
techniques.goal: Standardize capture workflows with RenderDoc/PIX/Ghidra-class tooling.

techniques.name: UI/HUD Anchoring
techniques.goal: Maintain cockpit readability while preventing HUD depth conflicts in seated VR.

techniques.name: VorpX Behavior Profiling
techniques.goal: Document VorpX-specific behavior, edge cases, and reliable startup constraints.

techniques.name: Performance Constraint Envelope
techniques.goal: Keep cockpit mode frame pacing inside comfort-safe limits under real workloads.

experiments.title: Starfield cockpit camera stability baseline
experiments.hypothesis: Cockpit camera injection can remain comfortable when rotational latency is bounded and hand/controller mapping stays native-feeling.
experiments.notes: Track nausea triggers, camera drift, and conflict points with ship HUD overlays.

experiments.title: Starfield stereo + VorpX compatibility triage
experiments.hypothesis: Stereo rendering can be made usable in cockpit mode by constraining VorpX profile behavior and bypassing conflicting post-process paths.
experiments.notes: Capture VorpX profile diffs and rendering artifact categories for reproducible tuning.

experiments.title: Starfield frame pacing guardrails
experiments.hypothesis: Comfort-first cockpit mode is achievable when CPU/GPU budgets are codified into a reusable constraint envelope.
experiments.notes: Define hard and soft performance boundaries with reproducible measurements.

integrationSeams: Memory seam: findings can be serialized as memory candidates for future retrieval indexing.
Experiment seam: docs/experiment-logs and experiments/* are canonical drop points for run artifacts.
Pattern seam: modules/* folders are the reusable output contract for flat-to-VR techniques.
Game-lab seam: examples/starfield-vr and examples/rdr2-vr can evolve into game-specific research tracks.
Spatial seam: the future Quest surface consumes versioned canonical Stephanos projections and never owns separate goals, memory, approvals, execution queues, or evidence.
